Ability Score: One of the six statistics that determine a character's capabilities: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.
Armor Class (AC): A measure of how difficult it is for an attack to hit a creature. Higher AC is better.
Hit Points (HP): A measure of a creature's health and vitality. When HP drops to 0, a creature is typically knocked unconscious or killed.
Saving Throw: A roll made to resist or mitigate a spell, trap, poison, disease, or similar threat.
Spell Slot: A resource a spellcaster uses to cast spells. Spells of higher levels require higher-level spell slots.
Cantrip: A spell that can be cast at will, without using a spell slot, and without being prepared in advance.
Proficiency Bonus: A bonus added to d20 rolls for skills, saving throws, or attack rolls if a character is proficient with them. This bonus increases as a character gains levels.
Action: The primary thing a character can do on their turn in combat (e.g., attack, cast a spell, dash).
Bonus Action: A smaller, quicker action a character can take on their turn in addition to their main action, if a feature or spell allows it.
Reaction: An action a character can take in response to a trigger, even when it's not their turn.
